subject: LedgerWave — tool calls & deterministic output (recap + next steps)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@ledgerwave.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: LedgerWave — tool calls & deterministic output (recap + next steps)

Tom / Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Reconciliation failures: inconsistent classification across similar transactions leading to manual fixes (~7% of volume).
- Latency spikes during batch runs that block downstream reporting windows.
- Non-deterministic JSON produced by current assistant layer; engineering spends time normalizing outputs.
- Security: requirement for VPC-private deployment and audit-ready logs.

Current stack notes you mentioned:
- AWS EKS-based microservices, Postgres primary, Kafka event bus.
- A lightweight “assistant layer” that currently proxies to a variety of hosted LLMs (rate-limited).
- No prefix/KV caching today; token usage spikes on monthly reconciliations.

Success criteria you called out (verbatim/edited):
- Deterministic structured output for reconciliation events: schema validation pass rate >= 99.5%.
- End-to-end inference p95 < 200 ms for single-transaction queries in steady state.
- Ability to run a pilot on private deployment (VPC) and deliver audit logs + KMS integration.
- Measurable cost improvement vs current per-token spend (~target: 15-25% reduction using batching/caching).

Proposed pilot scope (initial ask):
- Implement 3 instrumented workflows: payment_matcher, dispute_triage, auto_categorizer.
- Redwood provides: model variant recommendation, JSON schema + validator, simple agent workflow wiring, and perf baseline.
- LedgerWave provides: representative sample data, staging creds, and a technical point-of-contact for infra access.

Attachments: I’ve attached a brief pilot scope workbook with the mapping we discussed. (ledgerwave_pilot_scope.xlsx)

Next concrete steps:
1) You to share a small sample set (payments_sample.csv) and confirmation of the legal/procurement path.
2) Redwood to send a pilot proposal and an engineering deep-dive agenda (we’ll include Rafael for cost/contract items and Monica for onboarding).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical session next week to walk through data shapes and infra access.

Proposed times: Thu Aug 19 10–11am PT or Fri Aug 20 1–2pm PT — I’ll hold both tentatively.

If any of the above is off, call it out and I’ll update. Thanks again — excited to move this forward.

—
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

From: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@ledgerwave.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@ledgerwave.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LedgerWave — tool calls & deterministic output (recap + next steps)

Camila — thanks for the tidy recap. Couple of clarifications and a small correction on volume so we’re precise for sizing.

Clarifications:
- Monthly reconciliation payloads: we process ~8M transaction events/month; realtime single-transaction lookups are ~200 req/s peak.
- Determinism target: 99.5% schema pass is fine; for any failed outputs we must include a standardized error object so downstream services can route to manual review.
- Security: private deployment is mandatory for pilot. We need KMS, VPC peering (or Transit Gateway), and exportable audit logs (last 180 days).

I’ve attached a small anonymized sample (payments_sample.csv) and dropped the file into a shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e.

We’re available for a technical deep-dive next Tue Aug 17 9–11am PT. Sarah (CC) will own infra coordination and will invite our network/security lead if needed.

On procurement: we’ll need a pilot SOW and an estimate (not binding) of spend. If you can include anticipated infra footprint guidance (gpu type / egress / expected token volume), that’d be helpful for internal approvals.

Thanks — Tom
Head of Platform Engineering
LedgerWave

[Attachment: payments_sample.csv]
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@ledgerwave.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@ledgerwave.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LedgerWave — tool calls & deterministic output (recap + next steps)

Thanks Tom — appreciate the numbers, that helps a lot. We’ll update sizing and include a standardized error object in the schema.

Draft pilot plan and asks: 
- Redwood to deliver: a short SOW, an estimated cost range (pilot), and a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive agenda for Aug 17.
- Engineering asks: a staging EKS namespace and a short-lived service account/role for a Redwood engineer; minimal network access (ingress from our peering) to hit a test endpoint.
- Security asks: confirm your preferred KMS provider (AWS KMS or external HSM) and whether ledgerwave requires a dedicated HSM.

Example of the deterministic output we intend to validate (simple JSON schema output example embedded here):
{
  "transaction_id": "string",
  "amount": "number",
  "currency": "string",
  "match_status": "enum: [matched, unmatched, manual_review]",
  "confidence": "number (0-1)",
  "error": "nullable object {code, message}"
}

We will run an initial validator locally against the sample you dropped and report back pass/fail rates. Rafael — can you prepare a ballpark pilot estimate (GPU tier assumptions + egress assumption) and a short appendix on contract/terms for pilots? Monica — can you own the staging access / onboarding checklist and send over the data ingestion template?

I’ll attach a one-pager pilot proposal (redwood_pilot_proposal_v1.pdf) in a follow-up; HubSpot link to the draft deal is here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765.

If Aug 17 9–10am works, please confirm and I’ll send invites.

—
Camila

[Attachment: redwood_pilot_proposal_v1.pdf]

- I’ll send the data ingestion checklist and sample Anonymization guide by EOD today.

Tom — confirm who on your team should receive the runbook (security / infra / platform). I’ll add them to the Drive folder and the invite for Aug 17.

Cheers,
